In recent presidential elections, U.S. turnout has been around 61-67%.
That means roughly 1 in 3 eligible voters still do not vote, even in big years.
Midterm turnout is lower, around 50-53% nationally.
Primary elections usually draw only about 20% of eligible voters.
Turnout often drops even more in local and off-cycle elections.
In 2020, youth turnout rose, but still trailed older voters by a wide margin.
Education gaps remain large: college graduates vote at much higher rates.
Close elections are common, so small turnout shifts can change outcomes statewide.
